structured.approach: Attempt 3 fixes the single G1 refusal, and feat.brd is rewritten in full. SM-5 said "No existing function signature changes", which was stronger than the source. It now quotes the architecture rule exactly: "Keep every existing signature; add new functions". It says the new behaviour comes from four new functions (CR-2, CR-3, CR-5, CR-6). It names the one change to an existing function: CR-4 adds an optional `risk` argument to `build_explanation_request`, which feat.classification calls additive. That callers who don't pass `risk` get today's prompt stays assumption B-A6. I then searched the file for the same overstatement. Two more places made it, and I reworded both. The section 4 intro said "Existing behaviour is kept"; it now quotes the rule and names the two additive changes, CR-1 and CR-4, citing feat.classification. OS-6 now reads "Changes to existing signatures beyond the two additive changes named in section 4". Everything else carries over from attempt 2: the file: citation form, the corrected SM-3, the template-ordered sections, the business question set and the validation check.

claims.text: The BRD follows the template sections problem, business outcome, users, scope, out of scope, business rules, success measures, approvals.
The business need is: AP managers want to see which overdue invoices belong to vendors that usually pay late, so they can chase them first.
Fitment is Yes with reason code FIT-Y-ROADMAP, linked to roadmap item R-AP-12 'give AP managers earlier visibility of overdue payables'.
The REQ-03 fitment gate was approved by PM and Leadership.
The REQ-04 BRD gate is Leadership, and the owner of this step is PM.
Current capability: ap_aging computes aging buckets (current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+) for open invoices. Strategy: help finance teams pay on time and avoid late-payment penalties.
The architecture rule is 'Keep every existing signature; add new functions'. CR-4 adds an optional risk argument to build_explanation_request.
Only two changes touch existing behaviour, and both are additive: the paid_date column (CR-1) and the optional risk argument (CR-4).
Vendor risk is 'high' when predict_delay_days(history) > 30, 'medium' when > 10, otherwise 'low'. It uses no LLM.
The overdue list covers unpaid invoices more than 30 days past due, sorted by days descending then id. Vendors not in risk_by_vendor get 'unknown'.
The portal renders <table class="overdue-risk"> with one <tr class="risk-RISK"> per row, showing id, vendor, days and amount to two decimals, and an empty string when there are no rows.
Invoice amount is Decimal, 2 dp. JSON between services carries amounts as strings with two decimals. ap_portal is Node.js.
Monetary amounts use Decimal, never float, and Decimal arithmetic is kept.
No finance posting, authentication, tenancy or payment execution is in this change. Tier is T2, and the risk label is advisory only.
R-AP-14 (aging export) is out of scope. The regulatory 'Late' label (more than 60 days, REG-LPR-2026-4.2) is distinct from 'overdue'.
Assumptions B-A2 to B-A5 and B-A7 come from pre-backlog assumptions A-1 to A-5.
Boundary tests are required at exactly 30 days.
org.templates contains the templates but no separate business question set, although the brief describes it as holding one.

open_questions: OQ-B1 (PM / Leadership): Confirm the business meaning of 'vendors that usually pay late' and 'chase them first' in an AP context (carried from FQ-1).
OQ-B2: Keep 'overdue' (more than 30 days) and the regulatory 'Late' (more than 60 days, REG-LPR-2026-4.2) as distinct labels.
OQ-B3: The inputs define no business KPI. What business measure should define success?
OQ-B4: Confirm calendar days for days past due in overdue_with_risk (D-2026-031), with the 30-day boundary tested (L-007).
OQ-B5 (PM): Should one overdue definition be shared with ZD-48501 and ZD-48211?
OQ-B6: How should an unpaid row that has a paid_date be handled?
OQ-B7: org.templates holds no business question set. Should an approved set be added?
OQ-B8: Should renderOverdueRisk HTML-escape vendor names and ids?
OQ-B9: Should the risk level appear as visible text in the portal, or only as the row class?
OQ-B10: How should ap_portal (Node.js) format the two-decimal amount string without converting it to binary floating point (D-2026-044)?
structured.summary: I rewrote feat.brd in full to fix the SM-5 refusal. SM-5 now quotes the architecture rule exactly ('Keep every existing signature; add new functions'). It names the one additive change to an existing function: CR-4's optional risk argument on build_explanation_request. The same overstatement is also fixed in the section 4 intro and in OS-6. The rest is unchanged from attempt 2: the template sections, business rules BR-1 to BR-16, the business question set, assumptions, open questions OQ-B1 to OQ-B10, and the validation check. The check finds no decision-log conflict; its only gap is the missing business KPI. Nothing blocks.
